title: Tuberculosis drug reference — first-line and drug-resistant-TB medicines

primarySource.label: National Guidelines for Management of Drug-Resistant TB (NTEP, Nov 2024)

note: Paraphrased from cited sources; weight-band doses per NTEP Tables 3.6–3.8. Availability flags: 'available' = standard NTEP programme drug; 'unknown' = not confirmed for this deployment.

drugs.label: Isoniazid (H)
drugs.role: Core first-line bactericidal; high-dose (Hh) in shorter DR-TB regimen
drugs.doseRef: Weight-band per NTEP; high-dose H 300–900 mg by weight band (Table 3.6)
drugs.contraindications: Active drug-induced hepatitis; prior INH hepatotoxicity

drugs.label: Rifampicin (R)
drugs.role: Core first-line bactericidal/sterilising; retained in H mono/poly regimen
interactions: POTENT CYP3A4/P-gp inducer: hormonal contraceptives (failure), warfarin/DOAC (reduced effect), ART (dose/regimen change), many drugs

drugs.label: Pyrazinamide (Z)
drugs.role: Core first-line sterilising (intensive phase); component of DR-TB regimens
drugs.renal: Extend interval in renal impairment / dialysis (dose post-dialysis)

drugs.label: Ethambutol (E)
drugs.role: Core first-line companion; component of DR-TB regimens
drugs.renal: Extend interval in renal impairment (renally cleared)
drugs.contraindications: Pre-existing optic neuritis; inability to report visual changes

drugs.label: Bedaquiline (Bdq)
drugs.role: Backbone of all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens (BPaLM, shorter, longer)
drugs.doseRef: 400 mg OD weeks 1–2, then 200 mg thrice weekly to week 24/26 (extension per criteria)
drugs.renal: Caution in severe renal failure (SCr >3×ULN relative CI)
drugs.contraindications: Documented Bdq resistance; significant cardiac conduction disease / uncorrectable QT prolongation

drugs.label: Pretomanid (Pa)
drugs.role: Component of BPaLM/BPaL (≥14 y; paediatric use restricted)
drugs.contraindications: Documented Pa resistance; age/paediatric restrictions per NTEP

drugs.label: Linezolid (Lzd)
drugs.role: Core of BPaLM, shorter and longer oral regimens
drugs.doseRef: 600 mg OD (≥14 y); reduce to 300 mg only after 9 weeks for grade 3/4 toxicity (extends duration to 39 wk); paediatric by weight band (Table 3.5)
drugs.contraindications: Grade 3/4 neuropathy (relative); severe cytopenia (Hb<8, platelets<75k, ANC<750)
drugs.pregnancy: Lzd-containing shorter regimen may be used in pregnancy with monitoring

drugs.label: Moxifloxacin (Mfx)
drugs.role: Component of BPaLM (full course regardless of FQ resistance); longer regimen
drugs.doseRef: 400 mg OD; high-dose Mfx 400–800 mg by weight band (Table 3.7)
drugs.contraindications: Documented FQ resistance (context-dependent — retained in BPaLM); QT prolongation risk

drugs.label: Levofloxacin (Lfx)
drugs.role: Core of 9–11-mo shorter and longer oral regimens; H mono/poly regimen
drugs.renal: Reduce/extend interval in renal impairment (renally cleared)

drugs.label: Clofazimine (Cfz)
drugs.role: Component of shorter and longer oral regimens

drugs.label: Cycloserine / terizidone (Cs)
drugs.role: Component of longer oral M/XDR regimen
drugs.contraindications: Active psychosis/seizure disorder (relative); heavy alcohol use

drugs.label: Ethionamide / prothionamide (Eto)
drugs.role: Alternative to linezolid in shorter regimen; longer regimen
drugs.pregnancy: Avoid (teratogenic) — Lzd-containing shorter regimen preferred in pregnancy

drugs.label: Para-aminosalicylic acid (Na-PAS)
drugs.role: Longer oral regimen (when other drugs unavailable)

drugs.label: Delamanid (Dlm)
drugs.role: Longer oral regimen; paediatric alternative where Bdq restricted
drugs.doseRef: 100 mg BD (≥12 y); 50 mg BD (6–11 y) for 24 weeks (Table 3.7)

drugs.label: Amikacin (Am) / streptomycin
drugs.role: Longer regimen ONLY where guideline-supported / paediatric Bdq-restricted; not a casual choice
drugs.doseRef: Weight-band 500–1000 mg (Table 3.7); ≤10 mg/kg (max 750 mg) if >60 y
drugs.renal: Nephrotoxic — reduce/avoid in renal impairment; level-guided

drugs.label: Imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem (+ clavulanate)
drugs.class: DR-TB Group C (carbapenem, with beta-lactamase inhibitor)
drugs.role: Longer regimen ONLY where guideline-supported; always given WITH clavulanate (as amox-clav)
drugs.doseRef: Imipenem-cilastatin 1 g + 1 g BD, or meropenem 1 g TID / 2 g BD — each with amox-clav 875/125 BD (Table 3.7)
